rationale:
The requirement `requirements.sdk.validation-cache.node_data` has two obligations. An assigned handle returns its data, and an unassigned integer returns `None`. Both are tested and asserted.

- **Assigned handle returns its data.** `tests/contracts.rs#fn[clones_interning_the_same_data_concurrently_get_one_handle]` interns `Node(42)` from four concurrent clones of one cache. It then asserts `cache.node_data(ids[0]).as_deref() == Some(&Node(42))`. That checks the returned data is the interned data and is wrapped in `Some`. It also interns `Node(43)` and asserts the handle differs, so one handle isn't returned for all data.
- **Unassigned integer returns `None`.** `tests/contracts.rs#fn[saved_node_and_edge_inputs_survive_a_different_handle_allocation_order]` builds a fresh `ValidationCache` and asserts `fresh.cache().node_data(subject).is_none()`. `subject` is a handle assigned by a different cache and unassigned in the fresh one. The same test later interns `Node(2)` in the fresh cache, so the assigned and unassigned cases are checked within one scenario.
- **Indirect coverage.** Many test domain helpers call `node_data(...).unwrap()` on assigned handles. For example, `Application` in `tests/contracts.rs` calls it from `node_path`, `node_content` and `outgoing_edges`. These add indirect coverage of the assigned-handle case.

I found no further input classes. Larger unassigned integers are the same class as the tested unassigned handle. Both obligations are covered.

text: `node_data` returns the data associated with an assigned handle. An unassigned integer returns `None`.
pub fn node_data(&self, node: NodeId<D>) -> Option<Arc<D::NodeData>>;
